# Lab 2 {.unnumbered} :::: {.callout-warning collapse='false' appearance='default' icon='false'} ## [Caution]{style='font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.25em;'} ::: {style='font-size: 1.00em; color: #282b2d;'} This section is being revised. Thank you for your patience. ::: :::: Lab 2 introduces the[ `vetiver` package](https://rstudio.github.io/vetiver-r/) for modeling. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree(path = "_labs/lab2/") ## _labs/lab2/ ## └── model-vetiver.qmd ``` ::: ## vetiver basics {#sec-vetiver-basics} The `vetiver` package comes in both flavors: [R](https://vetiver.rstudio.com/) and [Python.](https://rstudio.github.io/vetiver-python/). We'll use the reticulate package below to install the other packages in the `model-vetiver.qmd` lab. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(reticulate) use_virtualenv("myenv", required = TRUE) virtualenv_install( envname = "myenv", packages = c("palmerpenguins", "pandas", "numpy", "scikit-learn", "duckdb", "vetiver", "pins")) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} from palmerpenguins import load_penguins from pandas import get_dummies import numpy as np from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression from sklearn import preprocessing import duckdb ``` ::: ## Using `duckdb` The code below establishes a connection to a `duckdb` database. :::: {.callout-important collapse='true' appearance='default' icon='false'} ## [`duckdb` error]{style='font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.25em;'} ::: {style='font-size: 1.00em; color: #282b2d;'} This originally returned an error: ``` Traceback (most recent call last): File "", line 1, in duckdb.duckdb.InvalidInputException: Invalid Input Error: Python Object "penguins" of type "module" found on line ":1" not suitable for replacement scans. Make sure that "penguins" is either a pandas.DataFrame, duckdb.DuckDBPyRelation, pyarrow Table, Dataset, RecordBatchReader, Scanner, or NumPy ndarrays with supported format Traceback (most recent call last): File "", line 1, in NameError: name 'df' is not defined ``` ::: :::: Below we **load the penguins data** and **connect to DuckDB and create the table**: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} penguins_data = load_penguins() con = duckdb.connect('my-db.duckdb') ``` ::: The `load_penguins()` function put the penguins data into a DataFrame, then we can insert it into DuckDB *before* querying: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} con.execute("CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE penguins AS SELECT * FROM penguins_data") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ``` ::: ```{.python .cell-code} df = con.execute("SELECT * FROM penguins").fetchdf().dropna() con.close() ``` ::: Confirm the data: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} df.head(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` species island bill_length_mm ... body_mass_g sex year 0 Adelie Torgersen 39.1 ... 3750.0 male 2007 1 Adelie Torgersen 39.5 ... 3800.0 female 2007 2 Adelie Torgersen 40.3 ... 3250.0 female 2007 [3 rows x 8 columns] ``` ::: ::: ## Create `model` The model is created below (like lab 1). ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} X = get_dummies(df[['bill_length_mm', 'species', 'sex']], drop_first = True) y = df['body_mass_g'] model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y) ``` ::: ## Model information This will print the model information. ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} print(f"R^2 {model.score(X,y)}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` R^2 0.8555368759537614 ``` ::: ```{.python .cell-code} print(f"Intercept {model.intercept_}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Intercept 2169.2697209393973 ``` ::: ```{.python .cell-code} print(f"Columns {X.columns}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Columns Index(['bill_length_mm', 'species_Chinstrap', 'species_Gentoo', 'sex_male'], dtype='object') ``` ::: ```{.python .cell-code} print(f"Coefficients {model.coef_}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Coefficients [ 32.53688677 -298.76553447 1094.86739145 547.36692408] ``` ::: ::: ## Turn into `VetiverModel` The model is created with `VetiverModel()`, which is a **wrapper class** that takes our trained machine learning model and adds important metadata and functionality for deployment and versioning. ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} from vetiver import VetiverModel v = VetiverModel(model, model_name='penguin_model', prototype_data=X) ``` ::: ```{=html} ``` ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'VetiverModel()' %%| fig-align: center %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"16px"}}}%% flowchart LR RawMod[Raw sklearn model] --> VMod["VetiverModel()
wrapper"] VMod --> ModMeta["Model + Metadata"] ModMeta --> Dep["Deployment Ready"] subgraph Vet["What it creates"] InSch("Input Schema") ModTypeInfo("Model Type Info") Ver("Versioning") Api("API Generation") Ser("Serialization") end VMod --> InSch VMod --> ModTypeInfo VMod --> Ver VMod --> Api VMod --> Ser %% style %% style RawMod fill:#FFF,stroke:#4CBB9D,color:#000,stroke-width:3px,rx:10,ry:10,font-size:16px style VMod fill:#FFF,stroke:#4CBB9D,color:#000,stroke-width:3px,rx:10,ry:10,font-size:16px style Vet fill:#FFF,stroke:#4CBB9D,color:#000,stroke-width:3px,rx:10,ry:10,font-size:16px style InSch fill:#FFF,stroke:#ff6f69,color:#000,stroke-width:2px,rx:5,ry:5,font-size:15px style ModTypeInfo fill:#FFF,stroke:#ff6f69,color:#000,stroke-width:2px,rx:5,ry:5,font-size:15px style Ver fill:#FFF,stroke:#ff6f69,color:#000,stroke-width:2px,rx:5,ry:5,font-size:15px style Api fill:#FFF,stroke:#ff6f69,color:#000,stroke-width:2px,rx:5,ry:5,font-size:15px style Ser fill:#FFF,stroke:#ff6f69,color:#000,stroke-width:2px,rx:5,ry:5,font-size:15px style ModMeta fill:#FFF,stroke:#ffcc5c,color:#000,stroke-width:3px,rx:10,ry:10,font-size:16px style Dep fill:#FFF,stroke:#ffcc5c,color:#000,stroke-width:3px,rx:10,ry:10,font-size:16px ``` ## `pins` boards In this version, we're going to save our `pins` board to a temporary location, but in the lab, we'll create the directory before creating the board. ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'board_folder()' %%| fig-align: center %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"16px"}}}%% flowchart LR BrdFldr["board_folder()"] --> FSI[File System Interface] FSI --> VerStor[Versioned Storage] VerStor --> MetaTr[Metadata Tracking] subgraph BF["What it creates"] DirStr[Directory Structure] VerCont[Version Control] PinMngMnt[Pin Management] end FSI --> DirStr FSI --> VerCont FSI --> PinMngMnt style BrdFldr fill:#FFF,stroke:#4CBB9D,color:#000,stroke-width:3px,rx:10,ry:10,font-size:16px style FSI fill:#FFF,stroke:#4CBB9D,color:#000,stroke-width:3px,rx:10,ry:10,font-size:16px style BF fill:#FFF,stroke:#4CBB9D,color:#000,stroke-width:3px,rx:10,ry:10,font-size:16px style DirStr fill:#FFF,stroke:#ff6f69,color:#000,stroke-width:2px,rx:5,ry:5,font-size:15px style VerCont fill:#FFF,stroke:#ff6f69,color:#000,stroke-width:2px,rx:5,ry:5,font-size:15px style PinMngMnt fill:#FFF,stroke:#ff6f69,color:#000,stroke-width:2px,rx:5,ry:5,font-size:15px style VerStor fill:#FFF,stroke:#ffcc5c,color:#000,stroke-width:3px,rx:10,ry:10,font-size:16px style MetaTr fill:#FFF,stroke:#ffcc5c,color:#000,stroke-width:3px,rx:10,ry:10,font-size:16px ``` In `board_folder()`: - The **Path** (`f"{temp_dir}/models"`) is where to store everything - **`allow_pickle_read=True`** allows reading Python pickle files (needed for `scikit-learn` models) ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} import tempfile from pins import board_folder from vetiver import vetiver_pin_write # use temp dir temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() model_board = board_folder(f"{temp_dir}/models", allow_pickle_read=True) vetiver_pin_write(model_board, v) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Model Cards provide a framework for transparent, responsible reporting. Use the vetiver `.qmd` Quarto template as a place to start, with vetiver.model_card() Writing pin: Name: 'penguin_model' Version: 20250808T113005Z-aba30 ``` ::: ::: `board_folder()` creates a **pins board** that sets up a storage interface to a local temporary folder. This creates a standardized structure for storing "pins" (data objects/models). ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} print(f"Model saved to: {temp_dir}/models") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Model saved to: /var/folders/0x/x5wkbhmx0k74tncn9swz7xpr0000gn/T/tmpfqdr8zgh/models ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="show/hide print_tree()"} import os def print_tree(directory, prefix="", max_depth=None, current_depth=0): """Print a tree structure of directory contents.""" if max_depth is not None and current_depth > max_depth: return items = sorted(os.listdir(directory)) for i, item in enumerate(items): path = os.path.join(directory, item) is_last = i == len(items) - 1 current_prefix = "└── " if is_last else "├── " print(f"{prefix}{current_prefix}{item}") if os.path.isdir(path): extension = " " if is_last else "│ " print_tree(path, prefix + extension, max_depth, current_depth + 1) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} print_tree(f"{temp_dir}/models") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` └── penguin_model └── 20250808T113005Z-aba30 ├── data.txt └── penguin_model.joblib ``` ::: ::: The board folder handles versioning automatically and manages metadata about what's stored. ```{.default} └── penguin_model # pin name directory └── CURRENT-DATE-TIME-aba30/ # version directory timestamp + hash ├── data.txt # model metadata └── penguin_model.joblib # serialized model ``` ## Turn model into `VetiverAPI` ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} from vetiver import VetiverAPI app = VetiverAPI(v, check_prototype = True) ``` :::
